subject: FastRetail: deployment-mode checklist & next steps for checkout SLA
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Josh Reynolds <josh.reynolds@fastretail.com>, FastRetail Platform Team <platform@fastretail.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 07 Mar 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: FastRetail discovery recap — checkout path constraints and next asks

Thanks again for taking the time today, Josh — quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Key points we noted on the call:
- Checkout path is the highest priority: hard SLA target for end-to-end p95 of 120ms (you mentioned preference for <100ms for critical flows).
- Typical request profile: steady-state ~80–110 rps, promo spikes up to ~600 rps for short windows.
- Average prompt length ~40 tokens; expected response ~70–120 tokens depending on model variant.
- Two classes of traffic: (1) synchronous checkout scoring (strict latency), (2) chat/async support (can tolerate higher latency and batching).
- Data sensitivity: PCI-adjacent; would prefer Dedicated or Private for isolation but open to Hosted if we can meet SLA & security controls.

Open asks for your team to confirm (would appreciate short answers inline):
1) Can you confirm peak sustained 1-min QPS and 95th percentile end-to-end latency target you want us to validate?
2) Are there regional constraints (US only) or traffic that must remain in specific AZs?
3) Is procurement open to a time-boxed Dedicated POC or would you prefer Hosted evaluation first?

Recommended next steps from Redwood:
- Quick sizing run: we propose a 2-week POC on Dedicated capacity to validate p95 under spikes (we can run the test harness with your replayed traces).
- If procurement needs Hosted price comparison first, we’ll provide an apples-to-apples cost/latency model and a mitigation plan (prefix caching, regional routing, autoscale policy).
- Deliverable: POC success criteria doc + cost estimate + rollout plan.

I attached a short post-call notes PDF with the rough checklist and proposed timeline. Can you (a) confirm the peak QPS, (b) copy your procurement contact if you want pricing early, and (c) suggest two dates next week for a technical deep-dive?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: post-call-matters.pdf (summary, checklist)

From: Josh Reynolds <josh.reynolds@fastretail.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: FastRetail Platform Team <platform@fastretail.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Mar 2027 09:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: FastRetail discovery recap — checkout path constraints and next asks

Thanks, Aditya. Helpful recap. Quick answers below — I’ve also attached a couple of latency snapshots from last weekend.

Answers/clarifications:
1) Peak numbers: sustained during promotions we saw ~540 rps for the checkout API (1-min sustained), with short bursts up to ~900 rps for 10–30s. For the POC we care most about the 1-min sustained peak and the burst behavior.
2) Latency SLA: end-to-end p95 target for checkout must be <= 120ms; preference is <= 100ms if possible. The p50 is less critical.
3) Region: US only to start — east and west traffic split roughly 70/30.
4) Security: procurement will want SOC2 evidence and IP allowlisting; we can share our vendor questionnaire if you have a templated response.

About evaluation approach — we’re open to a Dedicated POC because of the isolation ask, but procurement asked if you can provide a Hosted vs Dedicated TCO comparison (3-month and 12-month) that assumes caching on checkout and autoscale profiles.

I’m looping in procurement and platform here: procurement@fastretail.com for pricing discussions.

Josh
Josh Reynolds
Director, Platform Engineering — FastRetail
josh.reynolds@fastretail.com
Attachment: fastretail_latency_snapshot.png

On Mon, Mar 07, 2027 at 3:22 PM Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai> wrote:
> [post-call recap pasted above]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Josh Reynolds <josh.reynolds@fastretail.com>, FastRetail Platform Team <platform@fastretail.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FastRetail discovery recap — checkout path constraints and next asks

Appreciate the fast turnaround, Josh — this is perfect. Based on the numbers you shared (sustained ~540 rps, spikes to ~900 rps, p95 <=120ms requirement), our initial recommendation is:

- Run a 2-week Dedicated POC (reserved GPU pool) sized to handle 1.2x your observed peak (we’ll model 1,100–1,200 rps headroom for safety). Dedicated gives predictable p95 under high concurrency and easier compliance evidence.
- Parallel cost comparison: we’ll produce a Hosted vs Dedicated TCO (3mo & 12mo) that includes caching assumptions and a best-effort latency profile for Hosted with autoscale + region routing.
- Fallback strategy: use Hosted for non-critical traffic (chat/analytics), Dedicated for checkout. We can also provision a lightweight regional Hosted fallback for burst overflow.

POC success criteria (draft):
- Sustained 1-min p95 for checkout <= 120ms under 1,100 rps sustained with bursts to 1,500 rps for 30s.
- No increase in error rate above your baseline (+1% tolerance).
- Integration checklist: auth & allowlisting complete, replay traces ingested, monitoring/alerts configured.

Next steps suggested:
1) Redwood to deliver: POC sizing worksheet + Hosted vs Dedicated TCO by EOD Thu (we’ll include quantization options and per-token estimates).
2) FastRetail: confirm procurement contact (copied) and provide replay traces + any existing WAF/CDN interactions that impact latency.
3) Schedule kick-off: propose Mar 22 or Mar 24 for 30–45m tech kick-off.

Attaching a proposed POC plan workbook — it has the sizing assumptions we’ll use. If procurement wants a draft contract addendum for a time-boxed Dedicated trial we can surface that too.

Thanks,
Aditya

Attachment: proposed-POC-plan.xlsx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: FastRetail — internal: POC pricing sketch and discount band ask

Internal notes (do not forward) — quick numbers to prep procurement reply: 
- Sizing: for 1.2x peak (~1,100–1,200 rps sustained) we recommend 6 x A100-equivalent GPUs in Dedicated pool with autoscale headroom for burst.
- Ballpark pricing (for discussion): Dedicated trial (2 weeks, reserved capacity): $38k–$55k depending on prepayments and burst insurance. 12-month commit (same capacity) amortized: ~$18k/month after commit discount. Hosted path (approx): $0.55–$0.85 per 1k generated tokens with caching assumptions lowering effective tokens by ~20% on checkout.
- Ask for discount band: procurement usually expects 20–30% for a multi-quarter committed trial; recommend we offer 18% for a 3-mo pilot commit, 25%+ for 12-mo.

Action items:
- Priyom: can you validate the GPU sizing + q8_0 quantization latency delta and confirm we can meet p95 <= 100ms with 6 A100-eq?
- Monica: please prepare a short SOC2 evidence pack and a templated vendor questionnaire response to send to procurement once they ask.

I’ll hold the two kick-off slots and wait for Josh to confirm.

— Aditya
